overview_markdown:
grip-ai is a self-hostable AI agent platform written in Python (~24k lines, 120+ modules) that positions itself as a lightweight OpenClaw alternative. Its core architecture is a dual-engine design: the Claude Agent SDK serves as the primary engine for Claude models, while a LiteLLM engine provides access to 15+ other providers (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, etc.). Notably, grip bridges its full 31-tool registry into the SDK engine as in-process MCP tools, so both engines expose the same tool surface — filesystem, shell, web search, Playwright browser automation, document conversion, and more.

Reliability is a clear focus: it implements real cross-provider failover via litellm.Router with per-deployment credentials, exponential-backoff retries, and per-call USD cost tracking. A single `grip gateway` process serves Telegram, Discord, and Slack channels, cron scheduling, multi-agent orchestration, and a REST API. The project ships via PyPI with an onboarding wizard that verifies API keys and fetches live model lists.

Compared to OpenClaw, grip is far smaller and younger — 11 stars, a single visible maintainer, and no community footprint (all Reddit 'grip' matches are unrelated). However, its engineering discipline is unusually strong for its size: 882 tests, a mypy-clean tree enforced in CI, and detailed changelogs. The main risks are the lack of documented sandboxing around its shell and browser tools, and the absence of any proven production user base.
